# Identifier API Reference (Java Version)

Based on the actual class definitions in the intra-mart Accel Platform core source (`im_core_base` / `im_core_impl` modules). Do not supplement methods from memory or guesswork.

## Package Structure

```
jp.co.intra_mart.foundation.service.client.information
├── Identifier          … Public API. The entry point for obtaining a unique ID
└── IdentifierSpi        … The Identifier service provider interface (an abstract class for swapping the internal implementation)

jp.co.intra_mart.system.service.information
├── SystemIdProvider     … An interface that provides a system-wide unique ID (the system ID)
└── SystemIdProviderImpl … The standard implementation of SystemIdProvider (im_core_impl module; communicates with the Server Manager)

jp.co.intra_mart.common.aid.jdk.util
└── UniqueIdGenerator    … A utility used internally by IdentifierSpi's standard implementation (generates an ID from a timestamp + sequence number)
```

## The `Identifier` Class

```java
package jp.co.intra_mart.foundation.service.client.information;

public final class Identifier {

    public Identifier();

    /**
     * Obtains an ID whose system-wide uniqueness is guaranteed, including in a distributed environment.
     * The generated string is 15 bytes long.
     * @return a unique ID
     * @throws IOException a communication error with the Server Manager
     */
    public String get() throws IOException;

    /**
     * Creates an ID that is unique within the application server.
     * Do not use this for anything other than processing that is closed within the application server.
     * Normally, use get() when you want to obtain a unique ID.
     * @return a unique ID
     */
    public static String make();
}
```

- A `final` class. Cannot be extended
- The instance holds no state (it has no fields). Instantiation is only needed when calling `get()`
- At class initialization time (in a static initializer), it detects a `SystemIdProvider` implementation via `ServiceLoader`, loads `identifier-config.xml` (described later) via `ConfigurationLoader`, and determines the `IdentifierSpi` implementation instance to use. **Application developers never interact with this initialization process directly**

### Internal Behavior of `get()`

```
get() {
    return make().concat(Identifier.provider.getSystemId());
}
```

It concatenates the 2-byte system ID returned by `SystemIdProvider#getSystemId()` onto the 13-byte string generated by `make()`, returning a 15-byte string. Because `getSystemId()` communicates with the Server Manager to obtain a system-wide unique ID, it throws `IOException` on a communication error.

### Internal Behavior of `make()`

```
make() {
    return identifierSpi.generate();
}
```

It delegates to `IdentifierSpi#generate()`. The default implementation (used when `generator-class` is not specified in `identifier-config.xml`) is defined internally as an anonymous class, as follows:

```java
private static IdentifierSpi newDefaultProviderInstance() {
    return new IdentifierSpi() {
        @Override
        String generate() {
            return UniqueIdGenerator.getUniqueId();
        }
    };
}
```

In other words, with the default implementation, calling `make()` is equivalent to calling `UniqueIdGenerator.getUniqueId()`.

## The `IdentifierSpi` Class (Service Provider Interface)

```java
package jp.co.intra_mart.foundation.service.client.information;

public abstract class IdentifierSpi {

    public IdentifierSpi();

    /**
     * Provides the implementation for Identifier#get().
     * Obtains an ID whose uniqueness is guaranteed. The generated string is 13 bytes long.
     * @return a unique ID
     */
    abstract String generate();
}
```

- Implementing the package-private abstract method `generate()` allows the generation algorithm behind `make()` to be swapped out
- Because `generate()` is package-private, **it is effectively impossible for application code to provide its own `IdentifierSpi` implementation** (it can only be extended/implemented from within the same package). Customization is only possible by pointing `generator-class` in `identifier-config.xml` at a different implementation class within the platform (not needed for ordinary application development)

## The `SystemIdProvider` Interface

```java
package jp.co.intra_mart.system.service.information;

public interface SystemIdProvider {

    /**
     * Returns a system-wide unique ID.
     * @return a unique ID
     * @throws IOException thrown if obtaining the ID fails.
     */
    String getSystemId() throws IOException;
}
```

- An SPI implementation detected by `Identifier`'s static initializer via `ServiceLoader.load(SystemIdProvider.class)`
- The standard implementation is `SystemIdProviderImpl` in the `im_core_impl` module (obtains a system-wide unique ID by communicating with the Server Manager)
- Application developers normally never implement or use this interface directly

## The `UniqueIdGenerator` Utility

```java
package jp.co.intra_mart.common.aid.jdk.util;

public class UniqueIdGenerator {

    /**
     * Creates a unique ID.
     * Generates an ID whose uniqueness is guaranteed for the current process.
     * The ID is composed of time information and a sequence number held by this class.
     * As a result, a different string is generated and returned as the ID on each method call.
     * The generated string is 13 characters long.
     * This method is synchronized in order to guarantee the uniqueness of the ID.
     * @return a unique ID
     */
    public static synchronized String getUniqueId();
}
```

- ID composition: the current time in `yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS` format converted to base 36, followed by a 2-digit base-36 sequence number (`00` through `zz`, incremented on every call, wrapping back to `00` once the upper bound is reached)
- Because it is a `synchronized` method, calls within the same JVM are thread-safe, but it can become a lock-contention bottleneck under high-frequency consecutive calls
- **Application developers do not need to call this class directly.** Use it via `Identifier.make()`

## `identifier-config.xml` (Platform Configuration)

```xml
<identifier-config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xmlns="http://intra-mart.co.jp/foundation/identifier/identifier-config"
    xsi:schemaLocation="http://intra-mart.co.jp/foundation/identifier/identifier-config ...">
    <!-- Specifying generator-class swaps the algorithm used by make() (unspecified by default) -->
</identifier-config>
```

- Specifying the fully qualified name of an in-platform class implementing `IdentifierSpi` in the (optional) `generator-class` element swaps the generation algorithm used by `make()`
- If unspecified, `newDefaultProviderInstance()` (the default implementation that calls `UniqueIdGenerator.getUniqueId()`) is used
- If the class fails to load (`ClassNotFoundException` / `InstantiationException` / `IllegalAccessException`), a `ConfigurationRuntimeException` (a runtime exception) is thrown, and initialization of the `Identifier` class itself fails
- **Do not edit this configuration file in ordinary application development.** Since it governs the platform-wide ID generation algorithm, if a change is genuinely needed, confirm the intent with the user and proceed carefully

## Usage Example from Actual Platform Code (For Reference)

`jp.co.intra_mart.system.workflow.engine.tool.EngineNumberingUtil#createNewNumber()` (`im_workflow_core` module, the workflow matter-number numbering process):

```java
public static String createNewNumber() throws EngineException {

    String newNum = null;

    if (UnitModeUtil.getInstance().isUTMode()) {
        // Fallback for execution environments that cannot reach the Server Manager, such as unit test mode
        newNum = Identifier.make();
    } else {
        final Identifier id = new Identifier();
        try {
            newNum = id.get();
        } catch (final IOException e) {
            throw new EngineException("IMW.SRV.ERR.0664", e);
        }
    }

    return newNum != null ? newNum : "N/A";
}
```

As this example shows, numbering business data (here, the matter number) should generally use `get()`, assuming a normal application execution environment (one that can communicate with the Server Manager). The fallback to `make()` is limited to special execution environments that cannot reach the Server Manager (such as unit tests); it is not something to imitate as a branch within ordinary business logic.

Other examples of actual platform code that use only `make()`:
- `jp.co.intra_mart.system.logic.log.LogContext#executionId` (`im_logic_impl`; the IM-LogicDesigner flow execution ID, used for in-process tracing)
- `jp.co.intra_mart.imbox.internal.util.DefaultIdGenerator#generate()` (`imbox_core`; internal ID generation)
- `jp.co.intra_mart.system.javascript.imapi.IdentifierObject` (`im_jssp`; the bridge implementation for the JSSP SSJS version of the Identifier object — the internal implementation used when the JSSP side obtains an ID equivalent to `make()`)

All of these are cases where "an identifier self-contained within a single process is sufficient," which differs in nature from a business data primary key, order number, etc. that requires avoiding collisions across a distributed environment.
